content.thinking:
The tool has a 180-second limit per command. I need to run tests in chunks (or in the background with nohup and poll). Let me run in the background, writing results to a file, and poll.

Let me restructure: run fuzz in background with output to a log, then check periodically.

Also let me speed up the fuzz: the reference DP is slow (Python, exhaustive). Let me reduce the reference cost by limiting R (small cases) and budget.

Let me first check how slow a single fuzz iteration is.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && cat > tmp/fuzzrun.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: fuzzrun.sh lo hi [opt] [log]
lo=$1; hi=$2; opt=${3:-1}; log=${4:-/workspace/tmp/fuzz.log}
python3 /workspace/tmp/fuzz.py $lo $hi $opt > $log 2>&1
echo "EXIT $?" >> $log
EOF
chmod +x tmp/fuzzrun.sh && time (python3 tmp/fuzz.py 0 8 1 2>&1 | tail -5)
